strings.md.title: Product handbook
strings.md.data.heading: Data
strings.md.data.note.nameRules: A table name appears in an application when, in a file of that application outside the migration directories, (a) a string is exactly the table name; (b) the table name comes right after FROM, JOIN, INTO, UPDATE or TABLE, or after TABLE, an opening parenthesis and a quote; or (c) the table name comes right after many2many:.
strings.md.data.note.comments: A name inside a comment counts as appearing.
strings.md.data.note.ormDefaults: Access through a model type, through a name put together from several strings, or through a library default such as the default table of an adapter, is not seen.
strings.md.data.note.onlyInMigrationsAnyRule: A name that appears only in migrations means none of these rules found it anywhere else. It does not mean the table is unused.

strings.md.dict.heading: Status dictionary
strings.md.dict.note.nameRule: A JavaScript object, and a TypeScript object that ends in as const, is read as a value set only when the name it is assigned to ends in Status, State, Type, Kind, Stage, Phase, Level, Role, Mode or Category, or in the plural of one of these (such as Levels or Categories), in any case. A value set with another name is not seen.
strings.md.dict.note.sources: The meaning of a value comes only from the code: the comment next to it, copied as written, and its display names, each with its place. A display name is an entry of a mapping table that has the member as its key, or, for a member whose value is an object, a message, label, name, desc or description of that object. Nothing is written by a model. A blank meaning means the code has none.
strings.md.dict.note.values: A value marked not computed is written as in the code (it refers to another constant or is an expression that was not worked out) and is not compared with the other side.
strings.md.dict.recognized: Forms of value set recognized in this version: {forms}.
strings.md.dict.form.goNamedType: Go named types declared as a string or an integer type (also in the alias form), with the constants of the same directory that are declared with that type
strings.md.dict.form.goTypedVar: Go variables declared with such a type and a value (var X T = value); a literal is the value, another expression is shown as written and marked not computed
strings.md.dict.form.tsEnum: TypeScript enum and const enum declarations
strings.md.dict.form.tsConstObject: TypeScript objects that end in as const
strings.md.dict.form.jsObject: JavaScript objects assigned to a const, let or var, to module.exports.X or to exports.X
strings.md.dict.form.jsRecordMember: members of such objects whose value is an object with a literal code, value or id (the first found, in that order), which is the value; the first string literal among message, label, name, desc and description is the display name
strings.md.dict.countLine: Value sets: {total} ({goType} Go types, {tsEnum} TS enums, {tsConstObject} TS const objects, {jsObject} JS objects). Members: {members} ({computed} computed, {notComputed} not computed). Comments: {comments}. Display names: {labels}. Same names with different values: {mismatches}. Skipped members: {skipped}.
strings.md.dict.countLineNotTaken: Candidates that are not value sets: {noConstants} Go types without constants or variables, {duplicate} Go types declared again, {untypedIota} untyped iota constants, {otherType} constants of another type, {plain} plain constants, {otherVar} variables of another type, {tsNoLiteral} TS const objects without literal members, {jsNoLiteral} JS objects without literal members. Mapping table entries that name no member: {unmatchedKey}. Mapping table entries that name more than one member: {ambiguousKey}.
strings.md.dict.mismatchNote: Value sets with the same name in two applications (ignoring case and underscores) are compared by value, not by member name.

strings.md.history.heading: Code health
strings.md.history.note: A script counts these numbers from the version history and the project files. They describe the history as it is.
strings.md.history.notWritten: The code health section was not written for this handbook.
strings.md.history.malformed: The code health file is not in the format this version reads.
strings.md.history.noHistory: There is no version history to count: {reason}. The test files below are counted from the project files.
strings.md.history.reason.notARepository: the project directory is not in a git repository
strings.md.history.reason.insideRepository: the project directory is inside a git repository that it is not the root of
strings.md.history.reason.noCommits: the repository has no commit under the directory
strings.md.history.yearsNote: The year is the year of the author time of each commit, in UTC. The Commits column counts each commit once; a commit that changes two applications is counted in each of them in the By application column.
strings.md.history.chartNote: The chart is drawn by a script from the table above.
strings.md.history.appsNote: Commits are counted without merges, in the directory of the application. Authors are the distinct author emails. The last column is the fewest authors, most commits first, whose commits make up at least 80% of the commits of the application.
strings.md.history.hotspotsNote: The score of a file is its number of commits times its number of lines at the latest commit. The 15 files with the highest score are listed. The features are the verified entries that quote a passage of the file. Git may not follow a file through a rename, so the history of a renamed file can start at the rename.
strings.md.history.uncertainNote: A count marked uncertain is for a file whose history branches: at that many commits git could not tell which file of the same name was changed, so the count can leave out or include those commits.
strings.md.history.coChangeNote: Two files are a pair when the same commits change both. A pair is listed only when its two files are in different applications, the pair was changed together in at least 3 commits, and a commit that changes more than 30 files is not counted. The 10 pairs with the most commits are listed.
strings.md.history.testsNote: A test file is a file in a source language whose name follows one of these conventions: {conventions}. A test that follows none of them is not counted. A source file is a file in a source language that is not a test file.
